would_have_shipped_defects.summary: The MeTTa suite named in the order was never run, yet the upstream filing tells the maintainer its result was revalidated at the new pin.
would_have_shipped_defects.why_blocking: The order's whole premise is that PeTTaChainer's own suite (test_forward_backward_compose.metta) returned empty in April; re-running it at 02a85c6 is the load-bearing evidence. The verdict lists that suite only as '(available in environment)' with no result, but the issue body sent to the maintainer states 'this revalidation confirms the issue persists at 02a85c6'. A maintainer reading the filing will believe their own suite was re-run at their sha when it was not, and the operator closing the April thread inherits an unbacked claim.

would_have_shipped_defects.summary: No test-suite output is recorded verbatim; the Python suite is a hand-written paraphrase rather than captured run output.
would_have_shipped_defects.why_blocking: The order requires results 'verbatim, per test'. What is recorded is an authored narrative per test ('Result: Empty (should return proof)', 'Issue: Derived facts not queryable') with a three-line counts block and no pytest output, no assertion text, no tracebacks. A later worker re-running the suite has nothing to diff against, and cannot tell a genuine behavioural change from a re-worded summary — which is exactly the failure mode (never revalidated for 3+ months) this order exists to end.
